  • Feelings of worthlessness (reinforced by hallucinatory content)  
  • Diminished ability to think or concentrate  

- **Psychotic Features:**  
  • Mood-congruent auditory hallucinations (“you’re worthless”) persisting throughout the depressive episode and predating it by 3 months  
  • No prominent mood-incongruent delusions or formal thought disorder  
  • Hallucinations occur in full consciousness, without clouding of awareness  

- **Exclusion of Alternative Etiologies:**  
  • No history of mania/hypomania → rules out bipolar disorder  
  • No delusions of persecution, control, or grandiosity → low likelihood of schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder  
  • Negative urine toxicology, no substance use reported → no substance-induced psychosis  
  • Normal TSH and CBC → no evidence of thyroid dysfunction or systemic illness contributing to psychosis/depression  
  • No neurological deficits documented → no focal organic cause identified  

**Clinical Severity:** Severe — evidenced by functional impairment (work concentration decline), persistent psychotic symptoms, psychomotor slowing, and profound anhedonia/fatigue. Insight and judgment appear impaired secondary to active psychosis.  

**Next Steps (Implied):**  
- Initiation of antidepressant + antipsychotic combination therapy (e.g., SSRI + second-generation antipsychotic)  
- Safety assessment reiterated (though no SI/HI endorsed, ongoing monitoring essential)  
- Consider outpatient psychiatric follow-up with close monitoring; hospitalization if deterioration or safety concerns emerge  
- Completion of pending labs (BMP, B12) remains appropriate but low-yield given current high diagnostic confidence  

This represents a prototypical case of unipolar major depression complicated by mood-congruent psychotic features — a treatable, biologically grounded condition requiring integrated pharmacologic intervention.
